texts: good. the find parses in full — the sixty-three feathers as a counted group, the base as part of the cliff, and day, year and morning all attached to the finding. One caveat that is corpus-wide and not fixable by rewording: "day 705 of Year 2" is stored exactly the way a day-of-month would be, so nothing downstream can tell it is a running day count.

bad: three separate things go wrong here — "about thirty" puts a fuzzy figure into a slot that takes only a whole number, "of that season" is attached to the falling rather than to the week and turns the season into a thing the time slot cannot hold (and there is no earlier season in the passage for "that" to point back at), and "normal" is dropped outright because typicality has no carrier there at all. Rewrite as "In spring, thirty feathers usually fall to the base of the cliff each week." — an exact count, a named season instead of "that season", and "usually" to carry the work "a normal week" was doing. Even after that, the translator can only tie one fixed thirty-feather group to a weekly recurrence rather than express a per-week rate over different feathers each time; that limit is ours, not your wording's.

good. the non-sighting is recorded as a proper denial of the whole "a heavy sky-cat hunt was seen" claim, dated to the night before the find and ordered before it, with the sky-cat hunt typed as a kind of hunt. The surface word "no" is not separately kept, but nothing the sentence claims is lost.

mixed: the report is sealed correctly and "might have molted" comes through intact, but two things are lost — the claim is never spread to the individual sky-cats, so a particular sky-cat can never be asked about, and "at the same time" is dropped entirely because simultaneity across several separate moltings has no representation. Rewrite as "Tessa Brae said that several sky-cats might have molted together." — "together" is the wording that is actually encoded as one joint molting, which carries the simultaneity and removes the need for the per-cat spread that is currently missing.

good. "the find" is correctly resolved back to the finding in the first sentence, so the recording attaches to that same event rather than minting a fresh one, and "recorded" leaves the find unchanged as it should.
good. "the feathers" resolves back to the sixty-three found earlier, the feather store is typed as a kind of store, and the store is recorded as the destination of the adding.
